title: Earth's energy balance
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:57Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, the Victorian physics card on the greenhouse effect, covers the mechanism of re-emission at a Year 11-12 depth rather than the Year 10 idea of energy in balanced against energy out, and a change of depth is not a small edit, so a new point is the safer choice.

draft.title: Earth's energy balance
card: Earth absorbs energy from the sun, mostly as light. The land, oceans and air warm up as they take it in.
Earth also radiates heat back out to space. When energy in equals energy out, the average temperature stays steady.
Greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide and methane, trap some of the outgoing heat in the atmosphere. This is the greenhouse effect, and it keeps Earth warm enough for life.
If greenhouse gases rise, more heat is kept than lost. The extra energy builds up and the planet warms.
draft.remember: Warming happens when Earth keeps more energy than it loses.

a.q: What happens to Earth's average temperature when it keeps more energy than it loses to space?
opts: It rises as the extra energy builds up
It stays steady as energy is shared out
It falls as the extra energy is used up
It rises only until the sun's output drops
a.why: Extra energy that is not lost to space builds up in the land, oceans and air, so the average temperature rises. It stays steady only when energy in equals energy out.
a.clue: Think about what happens to energy that cannot escape.

b.q: Over many years, a country burns large amounts of coal and the carbon dioxide in the air rises. Which change to Earth's energy balance does this cause?
opts: More outgoing heat is trapped, so less escapes to space
The sun sends more energy, so more is absorbed
Less outgoing heat is trapped, so more escapes to space
The sun sends less energy, so less is absorbed
b.why: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas, so more of it traps more of the outgoing heat. Less escapes to space and the planet warms. The sun's output is not what changes here.
b.clue: Greenhouse gases act on heat leaving Earth, not on sunlight arriving.

a.best: It rises as the extra energy builds up

b.best: More outgoing heat is trapped, so less escapes to space
